chunks: Aḥmad ibn Abī ʿAbdillāh, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ḥafṣ ibn al-Bakhtarī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, concerning:
A woman dies while her brother and her husband are with her; which of the two is more entitled to perform the salat over her? He said: Her brother is more entitled to perform the salat over her.

Thus, the interpretation of these two reports is that they are a kind of taqiyyah, because they conform to the doctrines of the ʿāmmah. The first part of the Book of al-Istibṣār fīmā ukhtulifa mina al-akhbār is completed, and in the second part it is followed by the Book of Zakat, by the praise of Allah, His favor, and His excellent granting of success; and blessings be upon the master of the messengers, Muḥammad صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, and his good and pure ʿItrah.

key_terms.أَخُوهَا: her brother, identified in the report as more entitled
key_terms.التَّقِيَّةِ: dissimulation or precautionary conformity used in particular circumstances
key_terms.الزَّكَاةِ: zakat, the next book mentioned at the close of the volume
key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: the funeral salat performed over the deceased
key_terms.الْعَامَّةِ: the broader Sunni majority whose legal views are being referenced
key_terms.الْمَرْأَةِ: the deceased woman under discussion in the legal ruling
key_terms.زَوْجُهَا: her husband, one of the two claimants to priority

ai.seo_question: Who is more entitled to perform the funeral salat over a woman, her brother or her husband?
ai.summary: This report addresses who is more entitled to perform the funeral salat over a deceased woman when both her brother and husband are present. The compiler then explains that this and a related report are to be understood as issued by way of taqiyyah because they agree with the views of the ʿāmmah, highlighting the importance of reconciling narrations in Shia hadith scholarship.
